item.name: Mordred
item.dashboardStatus: Published - public; 0.2.7 pending review (submitted 2026-08-31, auto-publish on approval)

listing.description:
Mordred connects your browser to the Mordred-Hermes agent on your own Mac: chat with it, find what you did before, and approve Web3 wallet requests.

Use Mordred to:
• Connect to the Hermes on your Mac by just opening the popup (admitted once with Touch ID).
• Chat with Hermes and search the conversations and mail it has imported, by topic and event.
• Select text on a page to see related conversations, recommendations and a local translation from Hermes.
• Review website connection and signing requests before they are sent to Hermes.
• Keep wallet signing operations and private keys on the Hermes side.

Mordred requires Mordred-Hermes, installed on the Mac with Mordred.pkg. The interface is available in 25 languages.

privacy.singlePurpose: Mordred is a bridge between the browser and the user's own Mordred-Hermes agent on their Mac. Its single purpose is to let the user work with that local agent from the browser: chat with it, look up related past conversations and mail it holds (including for text the user selects on a page), and review and approve Web3 wallet connection and signing requests before they are forwarded to the local agent. Wallet signing keys stay on the Hermes side; the extension only relays user-approved requests. Every feature serves this single goal of connecting the browser to the user's own local agent.

permissionJustifications.activeTab: activeTab lets Mordred attach the current tab's address to a chat message sent to the user's local Hermes, when the user has turned that setting on (it is off by default). It is used only after the user opens the popup and grants no background browsing access.
permissionJustifications.alarms: The Manifest V3 background service worker uses chrome.alarms to schedule short, periodic housekeeping that keeps the connection to the user's local Mordred-Hermes agent healthy: retrying and re-establishing the local connection after the service worker is suspended, and refreshing pairing/connection state. Because MV3 service workers are frequently terminated, alarms are required to reliably resume this reconnect work without a persistent background page.
permissionJustifications.hostPermissions: Host and content-script access maps directly to the single purpose: http://localhost/* and http://127.0.0.1/* allow WebSocket data exchange with the user's local Mordred-Hermes gateway on the port its installer chose (47711 by default). The http(s)://*/* content script is the selection panel: it does nothing until the user selects text, then sends that selection to the local Hermes and shows the related results in a panel on the page. https://*/* and localhost content-script matches also make a lightweight Web3 provider available so a page can request a wallet connection. No site can access an account or request a signature until the user explicitly approves it in Mordred, and wallet keys never leave the local Hermes agent.
permissionJustifications.nativeMessaging: nativeMessaging talks only to the native host com.mordred.hermes that the Mordred-Hermes installer registers on the user's Mac. Mordred asks it for the local Hermes address (so the user never types a port) and for a ticket that lets Hermes raise its Touch ID approval for this extension only. No page content is sent to the native host.
permissionJustifications.scripting: scripting is used once after the extension is installed or updated, to add Mordred's packaged selection-panel script (content-recall.js) to tabs that were already open, so the feature works without reloading them. No remote or generated code is injected.

remoteCode.evidence: All executable JavaScript is packaged in dist/. The package contains no eval, new Function, importScripts, or remotely hosted script reference. WebSocket traffic goes only to the user's local Hermes gateway (http://localhost or http://127.0.0.1, port 47711 by default), or to another Hermes address the user enters. chrome.scripting injects only the packaged content-recall.js file.
